title: Fallece en Melgar (Tolima), el expresidente Gustavo Rojas Pinilla.
text: Gustavo Rojas Pinilla fue un militar, ingeniero civil y político colombiano que ejerció la presidencia de Colombia entre 1953 y 1957. Asumió el poder mediante un golpe de Estado el 13 de junio de 1953, desplazando al titular Laureano Gómez tras una crisis política.

title: Vuelta a Colombia 1975 ganada por Rafael Antonio Niño.
text: Rafael Antonio Niño Munévar​ fue un ciclista de ruta colombiano, que compitió en las décadas de 1970 y 1980.​ Obtuvo el récord de ser el ganador de más ediciones de la Vuelta a Colombia y el Clásico RCN, las competencias ciclísticas más importantes de su país.

title: 28 de julio. Es abatido en Cali el jefe máximo del EPL, Pedro León Arboleda.
text: Pedro León Arboleda fue un político, periodista y guerrillero colombiano, cofundador del Ejército Popular de Liberación.

title: Secuestro de Donald Cooper, gerente de los almacenes Sears por el M-19. Con el dinero obtenido por el secuestro se abasteció el grupo en medicamentos.
text: Sears es una cadena estadounidense de tiendas departamentales fundada por Richard Warren Sears y Alvah Curtis Roebuck en el siglo XIX. Opera en México bajo Sears México. En el 2005, Sears formó una alianza con Kmart, creando la Sears Holdings Corporation.

title: 8 de septiembre. El ELN mata en un atentado al inspector general de las FF. AA. general Ramón Arturo Rincón Quiñónez.
text: Ramon Arturo Rincón Quiñones fue un militar colombiano. Fue General del Ejército Nacional de Colombia, asesinado por el Ejército de Liberación Nacional (ELN).

title: Independiente Santa Fe Campeón del Campeonato colombiano 1975.
text: Club Independiente Santa Fe,​ también conocido simplemente como Santa Fe, es un club de fútbol fundado el 28 de febrero de 1941 en el centro histórico de Bogotá, capital de Colombia. title: en Caracas (Venezuela) finaliza la Copa América y la selección de fútbol del Perú es campeona por segunda vez tras ganarle 1‑0 a la de Colombia.
text: La selección masculina de fútbol del Perú​​​ es el equipo representativo de dicho país en las competiciones oficiales de fútbol masculino. Su organización está a cargo de la Federación Peruana de Fútbol (FPF), creada en 1922, una de las diez federaciones miembro de la Confederación Sudamericana de Fútbol (Conmebol).

title: Apollo–Soyuz Test Project: An American Apollo and a Soviet Soyuz spacecraft dock with each other in orbit marking the first such link-up between spacecraft from the two nations.
text: Apollo–Soyuz was the first crewed international space mission, conducted jointly by the United States and the Soviet Union in July 1975. Millions watched on television as an American Apollo spacecraft docked with a Soviet Soyuz capsule.

title: Viking program: NASA launches the Viking 1 planetary probe toward Mars.
text: The Viking program consisted of a pair of identical American space probes, Viking 1 and Viking 2 both launched in 1975, and landed on Mars in 1976. The mission effort began in 1968 and was managed by the NASA Langley Research Center.

title: English-born comic writer P. G. Wodehouse is awarded a knighthood, six weeks before he dies in the United States.
text: Sir Pelham Grenville Wodehouse was an English writer and one of the most widely read humorists of the 20th century. His creations include the feather-brained Bertie Wooster and his sagacious valet, Jeeves; the immaculate and loquacious Psmith; Lord Emsworth and the Blandings Castle set; the Oldest Member, with stories about golf; and Mr.

title: Colin Dexter's detective novel Last Bus to Woodstock introduces his Oxford police officer, Inspector Morse.
text: Norman Colin Dexter was an English crime writer known for his Inspector Morse series of novels, which were written between 1975 and 1999 and adapted as an ITV television series, Inspector Morse, from 1987 to 2000. His characters spawned a sequel series, Lewis, from 2006 to 2015, and a prequel series, Endeavour, from 2012 to 2023.

title: Barbara Pym and Philip Larkin meet in person for the first time, at the Randolph Hotel, Oxford, after years of correspondence.
text: The Randolph Hotel, also known as The Randolph Hotel by Graduate Hotels, is a 5-star hotel in Oxford, England, on the south side of Beaumont Street, at the corner with Magdalen Street, opposite the Ashmolean Museum and close to the Oxford Playhouse. The hotel building is in the Victorian Gothic style.

title: Harold Pinter's play No Man's Land is premièred by the National Theatre at The Old Vic in London, directed by Peter Hall and starring Sir John Gielgud and Sir Ralph Richardson.
text: Harold Pinter was an English playwright, screenwriter, director and actor. A recipient of the 2005 Nobel Prize in Literature, Pinter was one of the most influential modern dramatists of British theatre with a writing career that spanned more than 50 years.

title: Leftist Salvadoran poet, journalist and political activist Roque Dalton (born 1935) is assassinated by former colleagues in the People's Revolutionary Army (ERP). At the time, the ERP, was torn by a bitter factional fight. Dalton…
text: Salvadoran literature is primary literature written in El Salvador. Salvadoran literature is primary written in Spanish and in other languages like English.

title: As the 20-year time limit stipulated by Thomas Mann at his death expires, sealed packets of 32 of the author's notebooks are opened in Zürich, Switzerland.
text: Paul Thomas Mann was a German novelist, short story writer, social critic, philanthropist, essayist, and the 1929 Nobel Prize in Literature laureate. His highly symbolic and ironic epic novels and novellas are noted for their insight into the psychology of the artist and the intellectual.

title: Writing as Émile Ajar, the author Romain Gary becomes the only person to win the Prix Goncourt twice.
text: Romain Gary, also known by the pen name Émile Ajar, was a Lithuanian-born French novelist, diplomat, film director, and military aviator. He is the only author to have won the Prix Goncourt twice (once under a pen name).

title: Rembrandt's painting The Night Watch is slashed a dozen times at the Rijksmuseum in Amsterdam.
text: Rembrandt Harmenszoon van Rijn, known mononymously as Rembrandt, was a Dutch Golden Age painter, printmaker, and draughtsman. He is generally considered one of the greatest visual artists in the history of Western art.

title: The artists' community Kollektiv Herzogstrasse is founded by Heimrad Prem and others.
text: Heimrad Prem was a German painter born in Roding, Oberpfalz. From 1949 to 1952 he studied decorative painting at Schwandorf and then studied painting with Josef Oberberger and sculpture with Toni Stadler at the Akademie der Bildenden Künste, Munich until 1956.

title: The Brotherhood of Ruralists is established at Wellow, Somerset, England.
text: The Brotherhood of Ruralists is a British art group founded in 1975 in Wellow, Somerset, to paint nature. Their work is figurative with a strong adherence to 'traditional' skills.

title: Mona Hatoum leaves her native Lebanon to study at the Byam Shaw School of Art in London.
text: Mona Hatoum is a British-Palestinian multimedia and installation artist who lives in London.

title: Four Ronnie Landfield paintings from the collection of Philip Johnson are installed at The Four Seasons Restaurant in New York City, on the wall which Mark Rothko was initially commissioned to create paintings for, and subsequently changed…
text: Ronnie Landfield is an American abstract painter. During his early career from the mid-1960s through the 1970s his paintings were associated with Lyrical Abstraction (related to Postminimalism, Color Field painting, and Abstract expressionism), and he was represented by the David Whitney Gallery and the André Emmerich Gallery.
